methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center cohort design with 59 TNBC patients; post hoc power calculation demonstrates 88% power to detect observed survival difference but lacks prospective design and external validation. Cox proportional hazards assumption verified via Schoenfeld residuals; complete-case analysis applied despite 5-52% missing data for secondary variables. Univariate and multivariable analyses appropriately executed but no prespecification documented.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual retrospective cohort study (LoE 2b). CANT1 emerges as independent prognostic marker in TNBC, addressing documented clinical need for biomarkers beyond TNM staging in this aggressive subtype lacking established targeted therapies. However, mechanistic underpinnings remain speculative; no functional studies provided to establish biological basis for protective association with improved OS.

reporting_quality.justification: Biomarker prognostic study aligned with REMARK guidelines; comprehensive IHC methodology detailed (epitope retrieval, antibody catalog, staining protocol, controls), H-score derivation explicit, survival analysis methods clearly stated, clinicopathological and treatment data tabulated (Tables I–IV). Gaps include no REMARK checklist explicitly referenced, PD-L1/BRCA missingness not imputed, no external validation cohort. Data availability: no statement regarding raw data or code repository access.

novelty_literature.justification: First investigation of CANT1 expression in TNBC specifically; authors explicitly state prior absence of CANT1 characterization in breast cancer. Extends known context-dependent CANT1 biology (favorable prognostic effect reported in prostate cancer; adverse effects in HCC and lung adenocarcinoma) to novel tumor type. Represents meaningful extension of established CANT1 literature but not first-in-class discovery or novel mechanism.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear narrative arc from clinical need through methods, results, and discussion. Abstract, introduction, and methods section establish knowledge gap effectively; results section integrates figures (Figs 1–4) and tables (Tables I–IV) with clear presentation of H-score distributions, survival curves, and multivariable results. Minor typographical errors ('assocaited,' 'staing') and some repetitive phrasing in discussion, but overall publication-ready with effective communication of findings.

key_strengths: First CANT1 assessment in TNBC addresses unmet biomarker need in aggressive subtype lacking targeted therapies
Rigorous IHC protocol with automated staining system, blinded dual-pathologist scoring, and comprehensive quality controls minimizing technical variability
CANT1 association with improved OS retained as independent predictor in multivariable Cox analysis adjusting for age and other covariates
Inverse correlation between CANT1 expression and Ki-67 proliferation index provides biological plausibility for protective survival effect
key_concerns: Small single-center sample (n=59) with selection bias risk and inadequate power for covariate-rich multivariable models; no external validation cohort provided
Retrospective design with 5–52% missing data for secondary endpoints (PD-L1 52.5%, BRCA 59.3%, Ki-67 5.1%) and no sensitivity analyses for impact of missingness
Mechanisms underlying protective CANT1 effect remain speculative; no functional (in vitro/in vivo) studies or transcriptomic validation provided to establish biological basis
Context-dependent CANT1 prognostic effects across tumor types (favorable in prostate, adverse in HCC/lung) suggest finding requires independent multicenter confirmation before clinical adoption
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid exploratory biomarker study with rigorous immunohistochemical methodology and appropriate statistical analysis, but single-center retrospective design without external validation and small sample size limit tier placement to 3 (competent incremental contribution). Suitable for specialty journals (European J Cancer, Cancers) after minor revisions addressing REMARK checklist completeness and data availability statement.
